verdict: This is the rare hackathon plan where the "wow" and the requirement are the same object: the must-have IS the 3D replay, the paths the picker walks ARE the Dijkstra/Held–Karp output, the boxes that fly ARE the annealer's state, and the heat IS the per-order path visits. Nothing is a skin over a library sample. The three must-haves of 4.2 are met literally as written (prep JSON with top-100/picks/orders; grid warehouse with racks, aisles, dock, animated picker walking aisles with live m/s counters; swap/drag + same-order replay + before/after + fast-movers-nearest-dock baseline), and all three watch-outs are addressed in code, not prose. Zero backend, deterministic, static on Vercel: the safest live demo of the twelve. Two things would make me lean forward after 30 demos: the annealer physically swapping boxes with its energy curve drawing itself while a human pauses it and argues with it, and the ghost race on the same real invoices. The evaluation design (chronological split committed first, ABC as the real baseline, routing-policy ablation, eval script = app numbers by construction, 5-seed mean±sd, in-sample vs held-out gap shown on purpose) is the most honest I have seen proposed for this problem. What stops it being a 9: (1) the schedule contradicts itself (mvp-m3 tagged at 01:30 while the swap UI and ABC baseline are scheduled 01:45–04:15), so the must-haves would land after the stretch goals unless reordered; (2) the single number the whole story rests on, SA vs ABC on the held-out half, is unmeasured and may be 1–3% under optimal routing, which turns "watch it think" into "watch it shuffle"; (3) the 5-minute script has ~20 operator actions and zero slack; (4) the rendering budget is violated by the plan's own choice of 100 troika Text meshes plus Bloom at 1.5 dpr on a projector laptop; (5) the explain-every-line requirement is a real exposure when four agents write ~5k lines overnight while the humans sleep. All fixable tonight; none is a reason to pick another problem.
fatal_flaws: Schedule contradiction puts stretch goals before must-haves: the plan tags mvp-m3 at 01:30, but Agent B's click-to-swap is 02:15–04:15 and Agent A's abcBaseline is 01:45–02:15, so M3 (player swaps + same-order replay + baseline to beat) cannot be demonstrable before ~04:30, while the annealer (a stretch) is scheduled to be live at 03:30. The rules say complete the three mandatory requirements before any stretch goal; a progress review at 02:00 would show a 3D scene with no game. Reorder: Agent B does boxes + click-select/click-swap (no DragControls, no tweens) immediately after the scaffold (by ~00:30); Agent A ships simulate.ts + abcBaseline before route heuristics beyond Held–Karp; worker SCORE/ABC before ANNEAL. Target mvp-m3 at 02:30, annealer after.

The payoff number is unmeasured: SA vs ABC on the HELD-OUT half under optimal (Held–Karp) routing is the entire justification for WOW 1 and the 2.5 h of delta-evaluation machinery. With 7-bay (10.5 m) aisles, one dock and 100 SKUs in 112 slots, ABC/COI is a strong baseline and optimal routing already compensates for scattered slots; a plausible outcome is 1–3% on held-out. Mitigation that must be decided by 03:30 with a headless run: (a) also run SA with the S-shape objective (route cost is O(aisles), so SA is faster) where affinity slotting matters most and report both; (b) if gain under optimal routing is <3%, lead the pitch with the S-shape number and the policy ablation and present co-op SA as 'measured, modest, explained' rather than as the headline; never headline Original→X (StockCode-sorted original is arbitrary and the 30–50% number it produces will be read as a rigged baseline).

Rendering budget is violated by the plan's own choices: drei <Text> (troika) is one mesh and one draw call per label, so 100 StockCode labels alone exceed the stated <150 draw-call target before racks, uprights, Line2, Html overlays and the picker; add Bloom (mipmapBlur) at dpr 1.5 on a 1080p projector laptop with an integrated GPU and the 'auto-drop below 40 fps' path will trigger during the demo, mid-camera-tween. Fix tonight: labels only for hovered/selected + top-10 by picks (or one CanvasTexture atlas on instanced quads = 1 draw call); default quality 'Low' (no Bloom, dpr 1.25) and treat 'High' as opt-in after a measured ≥50 fps on the actual demo laptop; cut N8AO and the ortho projection morph entirely.
weaknesses: Demo script is over-stuffed: seven segments, ~20 operator actions, three live computations, and exactly 5:00 with no slack. One missed camera tween or a slow annealer eats the Evidence segment, which is the one the 'fabricated results = disqualification' rule rewards. The 'Replay twice gives identical numbers' beat proves nothing (a deterministic replay with no RNG is trivially identical) and costs 10 s.

'Exact per-order routing so distances are a bound not a guess' is overclaimed: Held–Karp is only used for ≤10 deduped stops; the wholesale invoices with 15–40 covered lines use NN+2-opt and they dominate total km. A judge who asks 'what share of your km comes from exactly-routed orders?' gets an unprepared answer unless eval reports it.

Watch mode at ~30 moves/s starting at T0 (median uphill move accepted with p=0.5) looks like random shuffling for the 30 s the judge watches; the energy curve will wander, not descend. The judge sees chaos, not thinking.

Ghost race ambiguity: the race can animate maybe 3–6 invoices in 50 s, but the Δ% on screen is implied to be the full held-out set (~1,300 orders). If the counter mixes the two, the first Q&A question is 'is that number from the five orders I just watched?' and the honesty story wobbles.

Co-op inject semantics are undefined: after the human's manual move the annealer 'continues from the human's state', but 'Finish fast' reports best-so-far, which may be the pre-human state, so the human's contribution silently vanishes. The judge who dragged the box will ask 'did my move matter?'.

Pick-time dilution: with 8 s/line and ~4–6 covered lines per order, the fixed pick component (~40 s) is comparable to walking (~60–100 s at 1.2 m/s), so a 10% km reduction shows as ~6% time reduction. Two different percentages on screen with no explanation reads as inconsistency.

Explainability exposure: Held–Karp bitmask DP, SA with inverted index + stop-set memo + delta breakdown, all-pairs Dijkstra, R3F instancing, troika, Line2, postprocessing, camera-controls, zustand, worker transferables, motion, radix. Four agents write ~5k lines overnight; humans have 11:00–12:30 to learn it and also re-run eval and record. 'Every member owns a module' is a sentence, not a plan.

Integration risk: four branches share store.ts and the worker protocol, but the store shape and types are not frozen up front; the scene (B) and UI (C) both write to it. Merge at the first checkpoint will be the slowest hour of the night.

Data mirror details are wrong in the plan: on huggingface.co/datasets/vancevo/online-retail-ii all 8 columns are typed string (Quantity, Price, InvoiceDate, Customer_ID must be cast/parsed) and the repo states no licence (empty README), so the licence must be cited from UCI, not the mirror; the UCI page's suggested citation is 'Chen, D. (2012)', not 2019. Raw UCI zip is 43.5 MB xlsx if the mirror fails.

Geometry story is thin: 8 aisles × 7 bays with the dock front-left means ABC puts the top-16 SKUs in the first bay of every aisle; the only thing SA can exploit is aisle co-location of co-picked items. That is a crisp story, but nobody has prepared the one concrete pair ('22423 and 85123A are co-picked in 31% of orders; ABC put them in aisles 2 and 5; SA put them in the same bay') that makes it land.

A human cannot beat ABC by hand in 5 minutes, so 'a baseline to beat' is a wall unless the player starts from ABC and uses the hover lookahead; the script relies on one lucky drag during annealing rather than a pre-tested two-move sequence.
frameloop='demand' with continuous picker animation, worker-driven state and an EffectComposer is a well-known source of 'the canvas froze' bugs; on stage it is a liability, not a feature.
Follow camera for 10 s on a projector risks clipping through racks and motion discomfort; camera choreography is decorative, not evidence.

Decorative/scope items with no judge-visible payoff: N8AO, ortho projection morph, Or-opt, batch picking, two-picker congestion, second month, DragControls (click-swap is already the primary). Each costs explain-surface and merge time.
fixes: Reorder the build so M1–M3 are demonstrable by 02:30: Agent A order = prep.py → layout.ts (graph + Dijkstra) → route.ts Held–Karp ≤10 + NN+2-opt only → simulate.ts + abcBaseline → worker INIT/SCORE/ABC/PATH → then S-shape/Return → then annealer. Agent B order = scaffold → racks/floor InstancedMesh → boxes + click-select/click-swap → picker + growing path + counters → then ghost/heat/tweens. Tag mvp-m3 when a judge could play the game headlessly in the browser; annealer, ghost race, heat and inspector come after.

Freeze the contracts in the first 30 minutes: Agent D (or A) commits web/src/types.ts (LayoutCfg, Assignment=Int16Array, Params, Policy, ScoreResult, AnnealTick), web/src/protocol.ts (the worker message union) and a store.ts skeleton with a 50-order mock JSON, so B and C build against real types from 22:00. Add an eslint-free rule: only Agent A edits sim/ and protocol.ts after 23:00.

Run a headless SA vs ABC on held-out by 03:30 (npx tsx eval/run.ts --quick, 5k iters). Decision rule: if held-out gain under optimal routing <3%, switch the annealer objective and the pitch headline to S-shape routing (realistic for pickers, affinity matters more), and keep optimal routing as the ablation. Report in eval/results.md: gain vs ABC on tune and held-out for both policies, share of total km from exactly-routed orders, and SA runtime.

Rewrite the demo to five beats with slack (target 4:30): 0:00 hook with the ghost race already running (10 s, most legible moment first) → 0:30 one hero order with path drawing + hover cause card + flip Optimal→S-shape → 1:30 ABC baseline flies into place, KPI table fills (tune + held-out) → 2:10 annealer: start from a warm state (resume the shipped seed-42 run at ~60% of the schedule so the energy curve visibly descends), PAUSE, one pre-tested human move with the toast, RESUME, Finish fast to the exact table number → 3:30 Evidence panel for 45 s (commit hash, seeds, ablation, held-out < in-sample called out, Limitations read aloud) → 4:15 close with QR codes. Cut the month scrubber, the pick-time slider and 'Replay twice' from the live demo; put them in the 3-minute YouTube cut.

Make the ghost race honest by construction: two counter groups, 'This race (N orders)' and 'Full held-out set (headless, 1,3xx orders)', the second computed by the worker before the race starts; the race animates a fixed scripted set of 4 invoices from demo.json at replaySpeed ×8 with the multiplier shown on screen.

Define inject semantics and show them: on INJECT set best := current and start a 'since your move' delta counter; Finish fast reports best-since-inject and the Player row = annealer-from-your-state. Toast text must come from the DELTA breakdown, never hard-coded; the numbers in the demo_script (412 picks, 13%, −0.9 km) are placeholders and must be replaced by measured values in docs/demo/script.md after prep.py runs.

Draw-call budget: labels only on hover/selected + top-10 SKUs by picks (or a single CanvasTexture atlas on instanced quads); racks, uprights, floor tiles and boxes as four InstancedMesh; one Line2 for the path, one for the ghost; verify with r3f-perf on the actual demo laptop at 02:00; default quality Low; frameloop='always' during demo with dpr [1, 1.25].

Prepare the geometry story as a 2-D top-down diff view in the Evidence panel (ABC vs SA, boxes coloured by aisle move, co-pick lines for the top-5 pairs) and one memorised concrete pair; this is the answer to 'what did SA change that ABC could not?'.

Explainability plan with teeth: each agent writes docs/explain/<module>.md (≤40 lines: what it does, the one invariant, the test that proves it, the two most likely judge questions with answers) at the moment the module lands; humans spend 09:30–11:00 reading those and running the tests, not polishing. Keep the Q&A cards to 10: top-100 coverage/truncated orders, why StockCode-sorted original, exact vs heuristic routing share, temporal split with repeat wholesalers, pick-time dilution, geometry, SA vs ABC mechanism, determinism/seed, limitations, what's next.

Data: prep.py must cast Quantity/Price to numeric and parse InvoiceDate from string (mirror columns are all string); log row counts after each cast and filter; cite UCI as 'Chen, D. (2012). Online Retail II. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5CG6D (CC BY 4.0)' with the HF parquet named only as the download path; record sha256 of the parquet in data/README.md; keep the 43.5 MB UCI zip as fallback.

Pin exact versions (no caret) for three 0.186.1 and postprocessing 6.39.5 because postprocessing's peer range is '>=0.168 <0.187'; a later three bump breaks install. Node must be ≥22.12 for vite 8.3.5.

Cut now, list under 'What's next': N8AO, ortho projection morph, Follow camera, Or-opt, DragControls, batch picking, two-picker congestion, second month, geometry sliders beyond the middle cross-aisle toggle. Keep: heat layer, leaderboard (localStorage), co-op inject, policy ablation.
Golf-style par HUD always visible in game mode: 'ABC par: X km held-out · You: Y km · −Z% vs par', so the game is legible in one glance and the player starts from ABC with a 'Start from par' button.
steal_worthy: Ghost race: a translucent picker on the old layout and a solid one on the new layout walking the SAME real invoices with counters diverging live; the most legible before/after any 4.2 team can show, transferable to 3.2 (uncontrolled vs scheduled load replay) and 4.3 (static plan vs re-planned routes).

Co-op optimisation: pause the optimizer, let the judge make a move, show the exact delta of that move, resume from the judge's state; works for any search-based problem (4.3 re-planning, 4.1 markdown steps, 2.1 slot assignment).

One pure simulation module shared by the Web Worker, the animation and a Node eval script, with the Evidence panel mirroring eval/results.md plus commit hash and timestamp, so README = app = deck by construction; this is the cleanest answer to the 'fabricated results' rule for any team.

Cause cards: every object on screen answers 'why are you here?' with counts from the data JSON (picks, distance to dock, co-pick partners drawn as lines) plus a one-move lookahead delta; a 10-line pattern that reads as explainability to judges.
Chronological held-out split committed in the data JSON before any optimizer commit, with the in-sample vs held-out gap displayed on purpose; cheap, honest, and visible in git history.
Worker message protocol defined in the first 30 minutes (INIT/SCORE/DELTA/ABC/PATH/EXPLAIN/ANNEAL_* with TICK events) so parallel agents build against a contract, not against each other.
Scripted hero order chosen by a script (8–10 covered lines across ≥4 aisles) and stored in demo.json, so the demo never depends on finding a good example live.
